cards: Herodotus was a Greek historian of the fifth century BCE, often called the father of history, whose Histories describe the peoples of the Persian world and the Greco-Persian Wars.
Thucydides was an Athenian general and historian, author of the History of the Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta.
Lysander was a Spartan admiral and statesman who won the Peloponnesian War for Sparta.
Xerxes I was king of the Achaemenid Empire from 486 to 465 BCE, the son and successor of Darius I.
Sophocles was an Athenian tragic playwright who lived from about 497 to 406 BCE.
Aeschylus was an Athenian tragic playwright, often called the father of tragedy, who lived from about 525 to 456 BCE.
Pindar was a Greek lyric poet from Thebes, the most admired composer of choral odes in antiquity.
Mahavira, born Vardhamana, was the 24th and last tirthankara of Jainism, a contemporary of the Buddha in the 6th or 5th century BCE.
Pericles was an Athenian statesman and general who dominated the democracy from the 450s until his death in 429 BCE.
Socrates was an Athenian philosopher who wrote nothing himself but questioned his fellow citizens about justice, virtue and knowledge, a method of inquiry known through the dialogues of his pupil…
Euripides was an Athenian tragic playwright, active from 455 BCE until his death in about 406 BCE.
Aristophanes was an Athenian comic playwright, the chief representative of Old Comedy, whose eleven surviving plays include The Clouds, The Birds, Lysistrata and The Frogs.
Pausanias was a Spartan general and regent for the young king Pleistarchus.
Themistocles was an Athenian statesman and general who persuaded Athens to build a large fleet with the silver of Laurion.
Ajatashatru was a king of Magadha in eastern India in the 5th century BCE, the son and successor of Bimbisara of the Haryanka dynasty.
Cyrus the Younger was a Persian prince of the late fifth century BCE, a son of Darius II.
Hippocrates was a Greek physician from the island of Kos, born around 460 BCE, who is traditionally called the father of medicine.
Bimbisara was king of Magadha in eastern India, ruling from Rajagriha, and a patron and contemporary of the Buddha.
c. 5th century BCE · South & Southeast Asia
Cimon was an Athenian statesman and general, son of Miltiades, who led the Delian League in the decades after the Persian Wars.
Phidias was an Athenian sculptor, regarded in antiquity as the greatest of the Greeks, who supervised the sculpture of the Parthenon under Pericles.
Theron of Acragas (died 472 BCE) was tyrant of the Greek city of Acragas in Sicily from about 488 BCE.
Darius II was a king of the Achaemenid Empire in the later fifth century BCE.
Leonidas I was a king of Sparta of the Agiad line who commanded the Greek force defending the pass of Thermopylae against the Persian invasion of Xerxes in 480 BCE.
Prasenajit, known in Pali as Pasenadi, was king of Kosala in northern India in the time of the Buddha, ruling from Shravasti.
Scyles was a Scythian king of the 5th century BCE whose story is told by Herodotus.
Alcibiades was an Athenian statesman and general and an associate of Socrates.
Bacchylides was a Greek lyric poet from Ioulis on the island of Keos and the nephew of Simonides.
Ezra was a Jewish priest and scribe who, according to the Hebrew Bible, came from Babylonia to Jerusalem in the Persian period with authority from the Achaemenid king Artaxerxes.
Goujian was king of the State of Yue from 496 to 465 BCE.
Heraclitus was a Greek philosopher of Ephesus who lived around 500 BCE.
Marquis Yi of Zeng was a ruler of the small Zhou state of Zeng, identified with Sui, in present-day Hubei.
d. c. 433 BCE · Central & East Asia
Simonides of Ceos was a Greek lyric poet from Ioulis on the island of Keos.
Teres I was the founder of the Odrysian kingdom of Thrace in the 5th century BCE.
Wu Zixu was a minister and general of the State of Wu, originally from Chu, who fled to Wu after the Chu king killed his father and brother in 522 BCE.
Amyrtaeus was an Egyptian ruler from Sais and the only king of the Twenty-eighth Dynasty.
Makkhali Gosala was an Indian ascetic of the 5th century BCE, the best-known leader of the Ajivika movement.
Wu Qi was a general and reformer of the Warring States period, born in the State of Wey.
Anaxagoras was a Greek philosopher from Clazomenae in Ionia who brought philosophy to Athens, where he lived for about 30 years in the circle of Pericles.
Artaxerxes I was king of the Achaemenid Persian Empire from 465 to 424 BCE, the son of Xerxes I.
Brasidas was a Spartan general of the Peloponnesian War.
